stem: Which of the following is a characteristic common to all living organisms?
options: They remain the same size forever
solution: All living organisms grow, respire, reproduce, need nutrition, excrete wastes and respond to stimuli.

stem: The process by which living organisms obtain and use food is called __________.
solution: Nutrition is the process of taking in and utilising food for energy, growth and repair.

stem: The process of releasing energy from food within cells is called __________.
solution: Respiration releases energy from food inside cells, usually using oxygen.

stem: The removal of waste products from the body is called __________.
solution: Excretion is the elimination of metabolic waste products from the body.

stem: A response of a living organism to a change in its surroundings is a response to a __________.
solution: A stimulus is any change in the environment; living things respond to stimuli (e.g., pulling a hand from a hot object).

stem: The basic structural and functional unit of all living organisms is the __________.
solution: The cell is the fundamental unit of life; all organisms are made of one or more cells.

stem: Organisms made of a single cell are called __________.
solution: Unicellular organisms, like Amoeba, consist of just one cell.

stem: Organisms made of many cells are called __________.
solution: Multicellular organisms, like humans and trees, are made of many cells.

stem: Which of the following shows movement but is NOT a living thing?
solution: A car moves but does not grow, reproduce or respire on its own — it is non-living.

stem: Plants make their own food using sunlight; they are therefore called __________.
solution: Green plants are autotrophs (producers) that make their own food by photosynthesis.

stem: Animals that depend on other organisms for food are called __________.
solution: Heterotrophs cannot make their own food and depend on other organisms; they are consumers.

stem: The growth of a living organism results mainly from __________.
options: an increase in the number and size of its cells
adding material from outside like a crystal
solution: Living things grow internally by increasing the number and size of their cells.

stem: The touch-me-not plant (Mimosa) folds its leaves on being touched, showing that plants can __________.
solution: Folding of Mimosa leaves on touch shows that plants respond to stimuli.

stem: Which of the following is used by most animals for breathing on land?
solution: Land animals such as mammals breathe using lungs; fish use gills.

stem: Fish breathe in water using __________.
solution: Fish extract dissolved oxygen from water using gills.

stem: Which process ensures continuation of a species from one generation to the next?
solution: Reproduction produces offspring, continuing the species across generations.

stem: The gas taken in by most living organisms during respiration is __________.
solution: Most organisms take in oxygen for respiration and release carbon dioxide.

stem: The gas released by animals and humans during respiration is __________.
solution: Respiration releases carbon dioxide as a waste gas.

stem: Which of the following is a non-living thing?
solution: A rock is non-living; the earthworm, mango tree and sparrow are living.

stem: A seed germinating into a new plant is an example of __________.
solution: A seed germinates and grows into a new plant, showing growth and reproduction in plants.

stem: Which of the following is characteristic of living things but NOT of most non-living things?
solution: Reproduction is unique to living things; weight, space and matter apply to non-living things too.

stem: Plants generally respond to light by __________.
solution: Plants show a response to light by growing towards it (phototropism).

stem: The variety of features seen among living organisms is called __________.
solution: The variety of forms and features among living things is their diversity.

stem: Microorganisms such as bacteria are living because they __________.
solution: Even tiny microorganisms carry out life processes like growth, reproduction and respiration.

stem: Which set correctly lists only life processes?
solution: Nutrition, respiration, excretion and reproduction are life processes; the others are physical/chemical changes.

stem: Amoeba, a unicellular organism, moves and feeds using __________.
solution: Amoeba uses pseudopodia (temporary false feet) to move and capture food.

stem: Living organisms need energy, which they obtain from __________.
solution: Organisms obtain energy by breaking down food during respiration.

stem: Which of the following statements about growth in living things is correct?
options: It is an internal, permanent increase up to a certain stage
It happens only by adding material from outside
It is the same as movement
It never stops in any organism
solution: Growth in living things is an internal process; it is permanent up to a certain stage of life.

stem: The blinking of the eye when a bright light shines is an example of __________.
solution: Blinking at bright light is a quick response to a stimulus.

stem: Which of the following organisms is capable of making its own food?
solution: Green plants make their own food by photosynthesis; animals cannot.

stem: A key difference between plants and animals is that most animals can __________.
solution: Most animals can move about, while plants generally stay fixed and make their own food.

stem: Excretion in plants includes the removal of gases such as __________ during the day.
solution: During the day, plants release oxygen as a by-product of photosynthesis, a form of gaseous excretion.

stem: The characteristic that helps us decide whether something is living is that it shows __________.
solution: Something is living if it shows the set of life processes together, not just a single feature like movement.

stem: Which of the following is TRUE about non-living things?
options: They do not grow, reproduce, or respire on their own
solution: Non-living things do not carry out life processes such as growth, reproduction or respiration on their own.

stem: Living organisms maintain their body and repair damage using nutrients from __________.
solution: Nutrients obtained from food are used for building, maintaining and repairing the body.

stem: A butterfly developing from a caterpillar is an example of __________ in a living organism.
solution: The transformation of a caterpillar into a butterfly is part of growth and development in its life cycle.

stem: Organisms that break down dead plants and animals are called __________.
solution: Decomposers, such as many bacteria and fungi, break down dead matter, recycling nutrients.

stem: Which of the following best shows that a plant is a living organism?
options: It grows, makes food and reproduces by seeds
It stays fixed in the soil
solution: A plant is living because it grows, makes food, respires and reproduces — not merely because it is green or tall.

stem: The set of similar cells that perform a particular function in a multicellular organism is a __________.
solution: A tissue is a group of similar cells working together to perform a function.

stem: Which of the following do both plants and animals require to live?
solution: Both plants and animals need air, water and nutrients to carry out life processes.

stem: The movement seen in a growing plant shoot bending toward light is an example of __________.
solution: Plants show movement in parts (like a shoot bending to light) though they do not move from place to place.

stem: Which of the following would you classify as living?
solution: Only the germinating seed carries out life processes; clocks, rivers and candles are non-living.

stem: The reason a car, though it moves and 'consumes' fuel, is not living is that it __________.
options: cannot grow, reproduce or respond to stimuli on its own
solution: A car lacks the life processes — it cannot grow, reproduce or respond to stimuli by itself.

stem: Which characteristic allows living organisms to adjust and survive in their surroundings?
solution: Adaptations are features that help organisms survive in their particular surroundings.

stem: In which way are all living organisms similar despite their diversity?
options: They are all made of cells and carry out life processes
They are all the same size
They all make their own food
solution: Despite great diversity, all living organisms are made of cells and perform basic life processes.

stem: A dead organism no longer shows __________.
options: life processes such as respiration and response
solution: A dead organism stops carrying out life processes, though it still has weight, shape and matter for a time.

stem: Which is the correct sequence in a simple life process cycle of an organism?
solution: Organisms are born or germinate, grow, reproduce and eventually die — the basic life cycle.

stem: Why is the ability to reproduce important for a species?
options: It allows the species to continue and not become extinct
It removes the need for food
solution: Reproduction ensures the species survives across generations, avoiding extinction.

stem: The presence of chlorophyll in a plant enables it to carry out __________.
solution: Chlorophyll captures light energy for photosynthesis, by which plants make their food.

stem: Which of the following organisms reproduces by laying eggs?
solution: A hen (a bird) reproduces by laying eggs; cows, humans and dogs give birth to young.

stem: A characteristic that distinguishes most animals from plants is the ability to __________.
options: move about in search of food
solution: Most animals move about to find food, unlike plants which make their own food and stay fixed.

stem: The overall message of the chapter 'Living Creatures: Exploring their Characteristics' is that:
options: living things share common features — cells, growth, nutrition, respiration, excretion, response and reproduction — that distinguish them from non-living things
living and non-living things are identical
solution: The chapter identifies the shared characteristics of living organisms that set them apart from non-living things.

stem: Things that show life processes like growth, movement and reproduction are called:
solution: Living creatures (living things) show characteristics of life such as growth, movement, respiration, reproduction, response to stimuli and nutrition, unlike non-living things.

stem: Which of the following is a characteristic of all living things?
solution: All living things share characteristics like growth, respiration, reproduction, movement, response to stimuli, nutrition and excretion, and have a definite life span.

stem: The increase in the size of a living organism over time is called:
solution: Growth is the increase in size and number of cells of a living organism over time; all living things grow, though in different ways.

stem: Living things produce more of their own kind by the process of:
solution: Reproduction is the process by which living organisms produce new individuals of their own kind, ensuring the continuation of their species.

stem: The removal of waste products from the body of a living organism is called:
solution: Excretion is the process of removing metabolic waste products from the body of a living organism, keeping its internal environment clean.

stem: Living things respond to changes in their environment; this ability is called:
solution: Response to stimuli (sensitivity) is the ability of living things to react to changes in their environment, such as light, sound, heat or touch (e.g. a plant bending toward light).

stem: The touch-me-not plant (Mimosa) folds its leaves when touched; this shows:
solution: The touch-me-not plant folding its leaves when touched is an example of a plant responding to a stimulus (touch) — showing that plants, like animals, respond to their environment.

stem: The process by which living organisms obtain and use food is called:
solution: Nutrition is the process by which living organisms obtain food and use it to get energy, grow and repair their bodies.

stem: Most animals differ from plants in that animals:
options: Move from place to place and depend on others for food
solution: Most animals move from place to place and depend on plants or other animals for food (heterotrophic), unlike most plants which make their own food and are fixed in one place.

stem: The basic unit of which all living things are made is the:
solution: The cell is the basic structural and functional unit of all living organisms; some organisms are made of a single cell, while others are made of many cells.

stem: Organisms made of only one cell are called:
solution: Unicellular organisms are made of a single cell (e.g. Amoeba, bacteria), which carries out all life processes; multicellular organisms are made of many cells.

stem: A car can move and 'consume' fuel, but it is non-living because it:
options: Does not grow, reproduce, respire or respond on its own
solution: Although a car moves and uses fuel, it is non-living because it cannot grow, reproduce, respire, respond or carry out life processes on its own — it needs a driver to operate.

stem: Living things need ______ to survive.
options: Food, water, air and a suitable environment
solution: Living things need food, water, air and a suitable environment (habitat) to survive, grow and reproduce.

stem: The definite period from birth to death of a living organism is called its:
solution: The life span is the definite period for which a living organism lives (from birth to death); different organisms have different life spans.

stem: The movement of the whole body or its parts is a feature seen clearly in:
options: Animals (and to a lesser extent, plants)
solution: Movement — of the whole body or parts — is a feature of living things, seen clearly in animals; plants show slower movements (like growth toward light or opening/closing of flowers).

stem: Which statement about living things is correct? (i) They are made of cells (ii) They grow and reproduce (iii) They respond to stimuli
solution: All three are correct: living things are made of cells, they grow and reproduce, and they respond to stimuli.

stem: Breathing in animals and gaseous exchange in plants are part of the life process called:
solution: Respiration is the life process in which organisms exchange gases (take in oxygen and release carbon dioxide) and release energy from food; all living things respire.

stem: Seeds germinate and grow into new plants, showing that plants can:
solution: The germination of seeds into new plants shows that plants grow and reproduce — key characteristics of living things.

stem: The main way to decide whether something is living or non-living is to check if it:
options: Shows the characteristics of life (growth, respiration, reproduction, etc.)
solution: To decide if something is living or non-living, we check whether it shows the characteristics of life — growth, respiration, reproduction, response to stimuli, nutrition and excretion.

stem: Some things, like a dried seed, appear inactive but are living because they:
options: Can carry out life processes (like germinating) under the right conditions
solution: A dried seed appears inactive but is living because it can carry out life processes and germinate into a new plant when it gets water, air and warmth.

stem: The variety of living creatures — from tiny microbes to huge whales — shows the ______ of life on Earth.
solution: The enormous variety of living creatures, from microscopic bacteria to huge whales and tall trees, shows the great diversity of life on Earth.

stem: Which of the following correctly matches a life process with its meaning? (i) Growth – increase in size (ii) Reproduction – producing offspring (iii) Excretion – removing waste
solution: All three are correctly matched: growth is the increase in size, reproduction is producing offspring, and excretion is the removal of waste.

stem: The overall importance of studying living creatures and their characteristics is that it helps us:
options: Understand what makes something alive, and appreciate and care for living things
solution: Studying living creatures helps us understand what distinguishes living from non-living things, appreciate the diversity of life, and care for and conserve living things and their habitats.

stem: A flame appears to 'grow', 'move' and 'need air', but it is non-living because it:
options: Does not reproduce, respond, or carry out life processes like a living organism
solution: A flame seems to grow, move and need air, but it is non-living because it does not reproduce, respond to stimuli, or carry out the true life processes that living organisms do.
